questions.stem: The bins are [0, 10), [10, 20) and [20, 30), where a square bracket includes the end value and a round bracket leaves it out. Which bin holds the value 20?
questions.explain: [10, 20) stops just before 20, and [20, 30) includes 20. A value belongs to exactly one bin.

questions.stem: A column holds the values red, blue, red, green, blue. How many distinct values (categories) does it have?
questions.explain: As a set the values are {red, blue, green}. Repeats are counted once, so there are 3.

questions.stem: A column x holds the values 4, 9 and 6. What does `SELECT MAX(x) - MIN(x) FROM t` return?
questions.explain: MAX(x) is 9 and MIN(x) is 4, so the difference is 5. This range is the denominator in min-max scaling.

questions.stem: A column x holds the values 2, 4, 6 and 4. What does `SELECT AVG(x) FROM t` return?
questions.explain: The sum is 16 and there are 4 values, so the average is 16 / 4 = 4.

questions.stem: A column dept holds CS, EE, CS, CS, EE. How many rows does `SELECT dept, COUNT(*) FROM t GROUP BY dept` return?
questions.explain: GROUP BY gives one row per distinct dept value. The distinct values are CS and EE, so 2 rows.
